{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past purchases and listening or viewing interests as continuing demand for broadly related items.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they extend a specific recent task, entertainment mood, or recognizable preference.",
    "Complementary items appeal when they add a clear capability to equipment or supplies users already own."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items compete with stronger matches despite requiring unsupported projects, incompatible equipment, or a different entertainment mood.",
    "Repeated interest is interpreted as demand for additional similar products without adequately accounting for recent ownership, redundancy, or replacement need.",
    "Historical preferences remain influential when recent behavior indicates a more specific current purpose."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Broad category, ecosystem, artist-era, and product-format similarity substitutes for matching the particular purpose or experience users seek.",
    "Purchases of accessories or supplies are generalized into demand for adjacent upgrades, specialized tools, or larger quantities."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Converging recent interactions identify specific tasks, moods, and combinations of preferences more precisely than broad historical interests.",
    "Compatibility, dimensions, capacity, quantity, and existing ownership determine whether an otherwise related product is useful now.",
    "Unclear item identity leaves relevance unestablished; passing on such items does not reliably indicate dislike."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The top recommendations too often establish broad relevance without establishing a specific current reason to choose, allowing speculative or redundant matches to crowd out actionable ones.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked recommendations users would choose now with an explicit connection to a recent task or desired experience.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to unsupported projects, compatibility mismatches, excessive scale, or already-covered needs.",
    "The frequency with which users prefer a lower-ranked specific match over a higher-ranked broadly related item.",
    "The frequency of unassessable recommendations due to insufficient identifiable item information, tracked separately from explicit mismatches."
  ]
}
